meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to think', paired with 'подумать'.

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'казаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to refuse, decline, renounce', paired with 'отказываться'.

examples.trans: He refused to sign the report.
Really? Did he refuse to sign it?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'call; bell' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Генерал Круглов ждёт звонка. Будьте любезны.
examples.trans: General Kruglov is waiting for a call. If you'd be so kind.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

придумать.gloss: to think up, to come up with

meanings.en: to think up, to come up with
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'думать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to think up, to come up with', paired with 'придумывать'.

examples.trans: You came up with this yourself!

examples.text: Как нет? Ты же сам это всё придумал!
examples.trans: What do you mean, no time? You came up with all this yourself!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'came', paired with 'приезжать'.

examples.text: Вика, ты на какой машине сегодня приехала?
examples.trans: Vika, which car did you come in today?
Why did you even come here? Empty-handed!

examples.text: Так, успокойтесь все. Сейчас за мной приедут.
examples.trans: Right, everyone calm down. They're coming for me any minute.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'ужели').

examples.text: Неужели так трудно найти хороший сюжет?
examples.trans: Is it really so difficult to find a good story?

examples.text: Неужели президент накажет вас за правду?
examples.trans: Will the president really punish you for the truth?
Do you really not care at all?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to leave, to go away', paired with 'уйти'.

Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to happen', paired with 'случаться'.

examples.text: Марина, я вам обещаю: со стеной ничего не случится.
examples.trans: Marina, I promise you: nothing will happen to the wall.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to make a phone call urgently.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно! Я должна вам сказать.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent! I must tell you.

вызывать.gloss: to cause, to raise; to call

meanings.en: to cause, to raise; to call
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'зывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cause, to raise; to call', paired with 'вызвать'.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, упаковка маскирующая. Не вызывает подозрений.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, the packaging is camouflage. It doesn't raise suspicion.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto; for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'work, job' in everyday Russian.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning '(emphasis) after all, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'time' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'until, before; up to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for; behind', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Common feminine noun meaning 'company, firm; group of friends' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And that is Osipenko's cousin's company!
He works at a large company.

examples.text: Не все компании такие добрые, как наша.
examples.trans: Not all companies are as kind as ours.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'all right, OK', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to give; (imperative) let's', paired with 'дать'.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'говориться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to agree, to arrange', paired with 'договариваться'.

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: From Latin 'momentum' (movement, brief span of time).

examples.text: А мне что-то уже не хочется. Момент упущен.
examples.trans: Somehow I don't feel like it anymore. The moment has passed.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'no ... at all, not any', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I have no money at all.

examples.text: Да нет у тебя никаких денег.
examples.trans: But you don't have any money.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'порт'). Common masculine noun meaning 'sport, sports' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Повара просят разрешить им заниматься спортом.
examples.trans: The cooks are asking to allow them to do sports.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('glad').

examples.trans: I'm very glad to see you.

examples.text: Ну что ты? Я очень рад тебя видеть.
examples.trans: Oh, come on! I'm very glad to see you.
